clue.text: birds live outside

definitions.note: NOT a definition: the source's clue has lost its definition, presumably an opening word meaning puzzle, so these wordplay words are all that remains

indicators.note: one thing sitting outside another wraps around it, so the word for live goes round the birds

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Some birds are living outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: As published, this clue has no definition: its first word, probably something like 'Puzzle', is missing from the source. The wordplay alone gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse someone is to puzzle or bewilder them, the meaning the lost opening word must have carried.

clue.text: 14s for Georgia in the course of being married?

definitions.note: plural, for a unit formed of battalions

indicators.note: something happening in the course of another lies inside it

blocks.note: a bride is a woman being married
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A wedding in Georgia involving 14s.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is BATTALION; a brigade is made of several battalions.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an army formation consisting of several battalions, so the battalions stand for the whole.

clue.text: Periodical parts of which are hot stuff

blocks.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical
the opening of the same word for a periodical, a further part of it

explanation.surface: A magazine some of whose pages are steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are bits of the word magazine: its first three letters, then its first two.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the earth's surface, literally very hot material.

clue.text: Part, maybe of 7, getting bad notices

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A platoon member gets poor reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is PLATOON; an army platoon is divided into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a part of anything, and in the army it is the subdivision of a platoon.

clue.text: Provide temporary accommo-dation for Mencap?

blocks.note: Mencap is a British charity for people with learning disabilities; its six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity is offered a place to stay for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram word; the question mark and the split 'accommo-dation' hint that letters are being moved about. Mencap is a UK charity for people with learning disabilities.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp troops is to settle them in tents or a camp, which is short-term lodging.

clue.text: Rivalry in handicrafts?

definitions.note: the tool used in such crafts

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... match is one fought with keen personal rivalry
second meaning: the sewing or knitting tool used in crafts

explanation.surface: Competitiveness among craftspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle is British slang for bitter rivalry, as in a needle match, and also the pointed tool for sewing or knitting.

clue.text: The largest 23, 'aving put my 'orn among the strings?

indicators.note: something placed among others sits in their midst, inside them
putting one thing among others means inserting it there

blocks.note: harps are stringed instruments; the Cockney accent drops the H
taken as written
a cor is a horn, as in cor anglais; the apostrophe mimics a dropped H
surface padding: having, said Cockney style, which signals that Hs are dropped

explanation.surface: A Cockney musician squeezes his horn in among the string section.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped Hs ('aving, 'orn) tell you to drop the H from harps. 23 down is GROUP: an army corps is a large formation of divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: An army corps is a formation of two or more divisions, among the biggest groupings in an army.

clue.text: Philosopher continuing with 23

blocks.note: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: A thinker who keeps going with his group.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is GROUP; a platoon is a small military group.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small army unit of a few sections under a lieutenant, one kind of military group.

clue.text: Itês ignominious when some of the French forget to come in ã but you could interpret it differently

indicators.note: some of a word is only part of it, so its tail is dropped
coming in means going inside, so these letters enter the other word

blocks.note: demeaning means degrading, ignominious
oublier is the French verb to forget

explanation.surface: It is shameful when French people forget to come in, though one could read that another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' means only the opening of the French verb is used. The clue's 'Itês' and 'ã' are the source's garbled apostrophe and dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A double meaning is an ambiguity, a phrase that can be read in two ways.

clue.text: Obtain acceleration from 21s

definitions.note: a phrase for the thing formed from squadrons

blocks.note: to win something is to obtain it
g is the symbol for the acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Getting a burst of speed from the 21s.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is SQUADRON. In the RAF, several squadrons make up a wing, part of the puzzle's theme of military units.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Air Force a wing is the formation built out of two or more squadrons.

clue.text: Gave me authority to enter fuel for proper feed

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so these words are placed within the fuel

blocks.note: coal is a fuel
OK'd, gave the go-ahead
taken as written
with gave, part of the phrase meaning approved, the OK

explanation.surface: Someone was authorised to put fuel on, perhaps to cook something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave' alone is too short: 'Gave me authority' reads as a single phrase, approved me, and the authority part is the OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked meal is a proper hot meal, as opposed to a snack; feed is informal for meal.

clue.text: Footballers in costume after game?

indicators.note: being in clothing means being wrapped by it, so the footballers go inside the garment

blocks.note: a sari is the draped garment worn by many South Asian women
the FA is the Football Association, the English game's governing body

explanation.surface: Players in fancy dress after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After game' looks like 'after the match', but game here means wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to hunt or watch wild animals, so it is literally going after game.

clue.text: Tautological bird, ill-clad, in footwear

indicators.note: something ill is in poor shape, so the following word is put into disorder
being in footwear means being enclosed by it

blocks.note: a boot is footwear
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sickly, poorly dressed bird in a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: The coot is the bird behind the saying 'bald as a coot', so calling one bald says the same thing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Coots have a white shield on the forehead that looks bare, so every coot is already bald: a redundant name.

clue.text: Amphibian embracing French maid in the hat that altered Dobson's poem

definitions.text: the hat that altered Dobson's poem

indicators.note: to embrace someone is to hold them inside your arms

blocks.note: a newt is a small amphibian
bonne is French for a maidservant

explanation.surface: A newt hugging a French servant who is wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin Dobson, a Victorian poet, wrote verse about a lady's new bonnet that changed everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Dobson's poem turns on a freshly bought headpiece, so the hat itself is the subject named.

clue.text: 19s are in, with acknowledgment to the king

definitions.note: plural, for a unit made up of companies

blocks.note: in cricket the side that is in is batting
ta is British informal thanks
the lion is called king of the beasts

explanation.surface: Companies join, giving thanks to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 down is COMPANY; a battalion is made of several companies. 'Are in' is cricket: the batting side is in.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an infantry unit formed of several companies, so the companies stand for the whole.

clue.text: Smile is right when in liquor

indicators.note: being in a drink means sitting inside it, so the letter goes within the spirit

blocks.note: gin is a spirit
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Smiling is the right thing to do when drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The source gives TRIN, which is not a word; the wordplay plainly gives GRIN, and the first cell is unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Used a pen when talking like a parrot?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for the noun, as in by rote

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard spoken rather than seen spelt

blocks.note: using a pen is writing; the past tense is wrote

explanation.surface: Someone who writes things down when speaking like a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means repeating mechanically without understanding, which is what a parrot does.

clue.text: Demand one right away before M-Mass

indicators.note: something taken away is removed from the word

blocks.note: to require is to demand
R stands for right; only one of the two is removed
the stammered first letter, taken as written

explanation.surface: A stammering priest demanding someone go right before Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one R (the last) out of REQUIRE, then add the M from the stammer before Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A requiem is a Mass said for the souls of the dead.

clue.text: Deferment of hope providing sad clue to earth?

blocks.note: first meaning: Proverbs says hope deferred maketh the ..., that is, sad
second meaning: split as two words it reads as a crossword clue, a word plus a word signalling that its letters are rearranged into earth

explanation.surface: Putting off hope makes for a sorry hint about the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Hope deferred maketh the heart sick' comes from the Bible. Read as HEART + SICK, the answer is itself a mini-clue: the letters of heart, sick (jumbled), make earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsick means deeply sad or despondent, an adjective matching sad.

clue.text: Enigmatist separates the men from the boys

definitions.text: separates the men from the boys
definitions.note: a phrase for one who sifts

blocks.note: first meaning: one who sets puzzles

blocks.clueFragment: separates the men from the boys
blocks.note: second meaning: one who sifts with a riddle, a coarse sieve, separating large from small

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter sorts the capable solvers from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is also a coarse sieve, so one who riddles sorts big bits from small: the men from the boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddler poses riddles, and also sifts with a riddle sieve, separating large pieces from small.

blocks.note: surface reading: two items numbered seven, or simply the number two
setter's reading: 7 down is a small army unit, and two or more of them form the larger one; also, as the saying goes, two's this

explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is PLATOON, and an army company is made of platoons. The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is an army unit of several platoons, and in the proverb two people make company.

clue.text: Ships' 19s reported journey

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: 19 is COMPANY, and a ship's company is its crew

explanation.surface: The sailors talk about their trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a voyage or journey by sea, usually for pleasure.

clue.text: Some fleet flying horse?

blocks.note: surface reading: a swift winged horse, like Pegasus
setter's reading: a unit of ships, of aircraft, or of cavalry; part of a fleet, a flying unit, or a horse unit

explanation.walkthrough: Fleet looks like the adjective swift; it is a noun, a fleet of ships. The word names a unit in all three services: navy, air force and cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is a detachment of warships, a unit of military aircraft, or a cavalry unit.

clue.text: Explorer Hammarskjold gets a degree

blocks.note: Dag Hammarskjold was the UN Secretary-General in the 1950s
taken as written
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A UN Secretary-General who travelled widely receives an academic qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who first sailed from Europe round Africa to India.

clue.text: 9s come to maturity when the West leaves

definitions.note: plural, for a formation made up of wings

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so the letter for West is removed

blocks.note: to grow up is to reach adulthood
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Wings mature once the West departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is WING; in the RAF a group is made up of wings.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Air Force a group is the formation above a wing, made up of several of them.

clue.text: What's the use of eyes in the face in relation to a 23 of 1 downs?

definitions.text: in relation to a 23 of 1 downs

indicators.note: being in the face means sitting inside it, so the first part goes within the second

blocks.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
the use of the eyes is sight

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why we have eyes in our faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is GROUP and 1 down is BRIGADE: an army division is a group of brigades, so the definition means relating to a division.
explanation.definitionFit: Divisional is the adjective of division, the army formation made up of several brigades.

clue.text: Exam in which a student gets gold

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written
L is a learner, from the L-plate on British learner drivers' cars

explanation.surface: A test where a pupil wins a gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets gold' means the gold is added; it goes in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as opposed to a written paper.

clue.text: Half grand clue of the day?

blocks.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
a key is a clue to solving something

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue half as good as its day's best one.
explanation.walkthrough: A monkey is British slang for 500 pounds, half a grand (a thousand).
explanation.definitionFit: In British money slang a monkey is five hundred pounds, which is half of a grand, or one thousand.

clue.text: Prize for solver's keeping the right to work

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the following letters are held inside

blocks.note: the solver is addressed as you, so solver's is your, archaic thy
R is the abbreviation for right
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: This is a prize puzzle: the winner keeps the right to carry on working.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle speaks to its solver as 'you', so the solver's is 'your', here the old form thy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or similar award given as a prize.
